headline: Equities edge higher as oil tensions overshadow steady open
deck: Markets post modest gains despite geopolitical friction pushing crude prices higher and weighing on futures.
body:
The broader market kicked off the week in the green, with the S&P 500 climbing 0.54%, the Nasdaq up 0.46%, and the Dow outpacing both at 0.94%. The broad-based rally suggests investor appetite remains intact despite headline risks, though the divergence in sector performance hints at selective positioning ahead of what could be a volatile week.

Oil price spikes tied to Trump's rejection of Iran peace proposals are creating cross-currents for equities. Energy stocks like Tullow Oil are benefiting from higher crude, while the broader market faces headwinds from elevated fuel costs—with Wall Street futures already reflecting weakness as geopolitical tensions flare. The standoff between the US and Iran is adding uncertainty to an already complex macro backdrop.

Meanwhile, the 10-year Treasury ticked up 7 basis points to 5.18%, signaling renewed inflation concerns and potentially limiting further gains in growth stocks. Supply shocks, from Qatar's delayed gas deliveries to Iran-linked disruptions, are reinforcing stagflationary risks that could keep momentum limited despite today's opening gains.
